ticket.title: TypeError when saving a product with a supplier ID returned as string
ticket.bug:
When PDO returns numeric database values as strings, saving a product with an associated supplier can trigger a `TypeError`:

```text
PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Domain\Supplier\ValueObject\SupplierId::__construct():
Argument #1 ($supplierId) must be of type int, string given

called in:
src/Core/Domain/Product/Supplier/Command/SetSuppliersCommand.php
```

The issue occurs while supplier IDs are processed by `SetSuppliersCommand`.

Depending on the PDO/database environment, a supplier ID can be returned as a numeric string, for example `"1"`, while `SupplierId` expects an `int`.

This is another occurrence of the numeric-string type issue tracked in #38735.

A similar occurrence was reported in #42447 and is handled separately by #42475 for the product grid and product pack flows.
ticket.steps:
The problem can be reproduced by forcing PDO to return fetched numeric values as strings.

Temporarily modify `classes/db/DbPDO.php` in the `getPDO()` method.

Replace:

```php
return new PDO(
    $dsn,
    $user,
    $password,
    $options
);
```

with:

```php
$pdo = new PDO(
    $dsn,
    $user,
    $password,
    $options
);

$pdo->setAttribute(PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES, true);

return $pdo;
```

This modification is only required to reproduce the affected PDO behavior and must not be committed.

Then:

1. Make sure at least one supplier exists.
2. Associate the supplier with a product.
3. Go to **BO > Catalog > Products**.
4. Edit the product.
5. Make any editable change.
6. Save the product.
7. Verify that a `TypeError` is triggered in `SupplierId::__construct()` because the supplier ID is provided as a string.

After the test, revert the temporary change to `classes/db/DbPDO.php`.

resolution.title: Fix supplier ID type in SetSuppliersCommand
resolution.description: Fixes a `TypeError` when supplier IDs are provided as numeric strings to `SetSuppliersCommand`. Supplier IDs are now explicitly normalized to integers before creating `SupplierId` value objects. |
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` variables are overwritten in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()`
ticket.bug:
There is a regression in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()` affecting the `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` hook.

This hook receives `$templateVars` by reference and is intended to allow modules to define or override template variables before the core assigns its general-purpose variables.

However, after the hook is executed, `$templateVars` is completely reassigned:

```php
$templateVars = [
    'cart' => $this->cart_presenter->present($cart, true),
    'currency' => $this->getTemplateVarCurrency(),
    'customer' => $this->getTemplateVarCustomer(),
    'country' => $this->objectPresenter->present($this->context->country),
    'language' => $this->objectPresenter->present($this->context->language),
    'page' => $this->getTemplateVarPage(),
    'shop' => $this->getTemplateVarShop(),
    'core_js_public_path' => $this->getCoreJsPublicPath(),
    'urls' => $this->getTemplateVarUrls(),
    'configuration' => $this->getTemplateVarConfiguration(),
    'field_required' => $this->context->customer->validateFieldsRequiredDatabase(),
    'breadcrumb' => $this->getBreadcrumb(),
    'link' => $this->context->link,
    'time' => time(),
    'static_token' => Tools::getToken(false),
    'token' => Tools::getToken(),
    'debug' => _PS_MODE_DEV_,
];
```

As a consequence, any variable added by a module through `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` is lost.

For example:

```php
public function hookActionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore(array $params): void
{
    $params['templateVars']['test_variable'] = 'test value';
}
```

`test_variable` is no longer available in Smarty after the hook execution.

This appears to be a regression from the previous implementation, where core variables were assigned individually using the existing value when already provided:

```php
$templateVars['cart'] = $templateVars['cart'] ?? $this->cart_presenter->present($cart);
```

That implementation preserved variables added by modules and also allowed modules to provide a value before the core calculated it.
ticket.expected:
Variables added to `$templateVars` from `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` should still be available in Smarty after `assignGeneralPurposeVariables()` has completed.

For example:

```php
$params['templateVars']['test_variable'] = 'test value';
```

should make the following usable from a Smarty template:

```smarty
{$test_variable}
```

Existing core variables provided by the hook should also not be overwritten, consistently with the previous behavior of this hook.
ticket.steps:
1. Install the [issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31307869/issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip) module.
2. Go to the Front Office.
3. In the footer, you should see the value value. Instead, **Variable not set** is displayed, indicating that the variable added by the module is not available in the template.

resolution.title: Fix #42395: Prevent template variables from being overwritten
resolution.description: This PR fixes a regression affecting the `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` and `action{ControllerName}SetVariablesBefore` hooks. Variables added to `$templateVars` through these hooks were lost because `$templateVars` was completely reassigned afterwards in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()`. The fix preserves the variables already defined by the hooks while still assigning the default Front Office template variables.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Install the [issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31308081/issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip) test module. 2. Go to the Front Office. 3. Check the footer. 4. Before this fix, `Variable not set` is displayed. 5. After this fix, the expected value `value` is displayed.
resolution.author: Codencode

resolution.title: Let a grid status menu show past the scrolling table
resolution.description: The order status menu in the Orders list is cut off when the list is short. The grid is wrapped in a `.table-responsive` (`Grid/Blocks/table.html.twig`), which Bootstrap defines as:  `.table-responsive { display: block; width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; }`  Once one axis is not `visible`, CSS makes the other one clip as well, so the container clips vertically even though only horizontal scrolling was asked for. With a few orders the table is only a couple of rows high, the status menu is taller than that, and the part that does not fit is cut - which is what the screenshot in the report shows.  The horizontal scrolling is still wanted for wide grids, so instead of dropping it the container is allowed to overflow only while a menu is open, and put back when it closes. It is scoped to the grid's own choice menus, so no other dropdown behaviour changes.  `data-boundary` was not the answer here: it changes where Popper positions the menu, not whether an ancestor clips it, so the menu would still have been cut.
resolution.how_to_test: Sell > Orders with only a few orders in the list, so the table is short. Open the status menu on a row: before this change the entries that do not fit inside the table are cut off; after it, the whole menu is visible and the table still scrolls horizontally when it is too wide.
resolution.author: boo-code

ticket.title: Pack stock type "Decrement pack only" is ignored by Pack::getQuantity() - empty() treats STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY (0) as "Default"
ticket.bug:
A pack whose per-product stock behavior is explicitly set to **"Decrement pack only"** (`pack_stock_type = 0`, `PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY`) is treated as if it was set to "Default" by `Pack::getQuantity()`, so its displayed/available quantity is resolved using the **global** `PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE` configuration instead of the pack's own setting.

**Root cause** - `classes/Pack.php`, `Pack::getQuantity()`:

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/classes/Pack.php#L293

```php
// If no pack stock or shop default, set it from configuration
if (empty($packStockType) || $packStockType == self::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT) {
    $packStockType = Configuration::get('PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE');
}
```

`STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY === 0` and `empty(0) === true`, so an explicit "Decrement pack only" is indistinguishable from "not set" and always falls back to the global configuration. The per-pack value 0 only "works" when the global default happens to be "Decrement pack only" as well. Values 1 ("products only"), 2 ("both") and 3 ("default") behave correctly.

The same line is present in all maintained branches:
- `develop`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/classes/Pack.php#L293
- `8.2.x`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/8.2.x/classes/Pack.php#L311
- `9.0.0`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/9.0.0/classes/Pack.php#L313

**Why this is more than a display glitch** - the stock *decrement* path uses exact comparisons and DOES honor the per-pack value 0 (`StockManager::updatePackQuantity()`):

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/src/Core/Stock/StockManager.php#L45-L70

So for a pack set to "Decrement pack only" while the shop default is "Decrement products in pack only" (or "both"):
- placing an order decrements the **pack's own** stock (per-pack setting honored),
- but the FO product page, listings, and availability checks (`Product::getQuantity()` → `Pack::getQuantity()`, `Pack::isInStock()`) display a quantity computed **from the pack's components** (per-pack setting ignored, global used).

The displayed availability is therefore computed from stock that is never decremented by sales of this pack, and the two numbers drift apart with every order. Since `Pack::isInStock()` relies on the same method, cart availability checks use the wrong mode as well - this may be (part of) the root cause of the overselling symptoms reported in #26728.

**Suggested fix** - stop treating the legitimate value 0 as "unset", while keeping the legacy NULL/empty-string fallback that `empty()` presumably guarded:

```php
if ($packStockType === null || $packStockType === '' || (int) $packStockType == self::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT) {
    $packStockType = Configuration::get('PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE');
}
```

**Related:** #26728 (open symptom report: overselling with "Decrement pack only" / "Decrement both"), #19846 (pack stock EPIC), PR #35372 (last refactor of this method, 8.1.5 - the `empty()` condition was kept unchanged).
ticket.expected: The pack's available quantity should be **1** - its own stock - because the pack explicitly overrides the shop default with "Decrement pack only". Ordering the pack decrements the pack's own stock, consistently with what is displayed.
ticket.steps:
1. Fresh PrestaShop install (reproduced on 8.1.7; the affected code is identical on `8.2.x`, `9.0.0` and `develop`), stock management enabled.
2. In BO: Shop Parameters > Product Settings > set **"Default pack stock management"** to **"Decrement products in pack only"**.
3. Create standard product A with quantity **10** and standard product B with quantity **20**.
4. Create a pack containing **2 × A** and **1 × B**. Set the pack's own quantity to **1** and set the pack's stock management option (product page > Quantities) to **"Decrement pack only"**.
5. Open the pack's product page in the front office (or call `Product::getQuantity($idPack)` / check the displayed availability).
6. (Divergence part) Place an order for 1 pack and compare which stock was decremented vs. which stock the FO displays.

resolution.title: Fix Pack::getQuantity ignoring 'Decrement pack only' stock type
resolution.description: Pack::getQuantity() resolved the pack stock type with empty($packStockType), which treats the legitimate value 0 (PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY, "Decrement pack only") as unset and falls back to the global PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE configuration. Displayed pack availability was therefore computed with the wrong mode, while the stock decrement path (StockManager::updatePackQuantity()) honors the per-pack setting, so the displayed stock and the actually decremented stock diverge with every order. This PR replaces empty() with explicit null / empty-string checks so an explicit "Decrement pack only" is honored, while keeping the legacy fallback for NULL values from old databases. |
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Shop Parameters > Product Settings > set "Default pack stock management" to "Decrement products in pack only". 2. Create product A (qty 10) and product B (qty 20). 3. Create a pack containing 2×A + 1×B, set the pack's own quantity to 1 and its stock management (product page > Quantities) to "Decrement pack only". 4. Open the pack's page in FO. Before this fix the displayed quantity is 5 (computed from components per the global setting); after the fix it is 1 (the pack's own stock — per-pack setting honored). |
resolution.author: samilmarekrygula

The bulk form submits this field as `[price][unit_price]` and `BulkCombinationFormDataFormatter` remapped it to `[price_impact][unit_price]`, but the combination command builder reads the unit price impact from `[price_impact][unit_price_tax_excluded]` (mapped to `setImpactOnUnitPrice`). The value therefore landed at a path nothing consumed and was silently dropped, while all the other bulk price fields (which map to matching paths) saved correctly. The fix remaps the bulk field to `[price_impact][unit_price_tax_excluded]`.
resolution.how_to_test: On a product with combinations, set a unit price + unity in the Price tab. In the Combinations tab, select one or more combinations, use bulk edit, and set "Impact on price per unit (tax excl.)". Before: `product_attribute.unit_price_impact` stays unchanged and the FO unit price is unaffected. After: the impact is saved and reflected in the FO. Covered by the updated `tests/Unit/Core/Form/IdentifiableObject/DataFormatter/BulkCombinationFormDataFormatterTest.php` (the bulk field now formats to `[price_impact][unit_price_tax_excluded]`).
resolution.author: boo-code

resolution.title: Fix TypeError on tax rules bulk delete when no rule is selected

The fix bails out early when nothing is selected (there is nothing to delete), which both removes the `TypeError` and avoids redirecting with a misleading "successful deletion" confirmation for an empty selection.

After: the action is a no-op (nothing selected, nothing deleted). Covered by `tests/Integration/Classes/AdminTaxRulesGroupBulkDeleteTest.php` (fails on the base branch with the exact `TypeError`, passes with the fix).

resolution.title: Fix: Module Development and Distribution: Prestashop deletes automatically src/Entity/index.php, but it does not recursively in subfolders
resolution.description: This PR fixes module entity scanning for API Platform when entities are organized in nested folders under `src/Entity`. Previously, PrestaShop only removed `src/Entity/index.php` before API Platform recursively scanned module entity resources. If a module also contained nested files like `src/Entity/Category/index.php`, those files were still required during resource discovery and could trigger redirects or exits, causing the process to fail. This change makes the cleanup recursive so all index.php files inside `src/Entity` are removed before the scan.

ticket.title: Carrier::getDeliveredCountries() uses wrong states ID resulting in wrong countries list
ticket.bug:
The new getDeliveredCountries() code has an error when fetching active states linked to delivered countries.
This is because when using the $countries array in `array_keys($countries)` its keys are in numeric order starting from 0, not using id_country as keys.
$countries has no id_country as keys. $result has them.
So `SELECT` is using `IN (0,1,2,3,....)` instead of correct country ids. This results in wrong countries list with countries without carries in it.
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/25f0ef48696506fcee01e34de069d0c7a3b7c144/classes/Carrier.php#L670
ticket.expected: Correct country list with ONLY countries with a carrier enabled.
ticket.steps: Just call the Carrier::getDeliveredCountries() function. You'll also get countries for which there aren't carriers available. For better proof, disable carriers for the countries with low states ID in them (like 0,1,2,3,4). They will be included anyway for the error explained in description.

resolution.title: Fix states lookup using row indexes instead of country IDs
resolution.description: `Carrier::getDeliveredCountries()` builds its states sub-query from `array_keys($countries)`, but `$countries` is the raw `executeS()` result with numeric row indexes (0, 1, 2, …) — not country IDs. Only `$result` is keyed by `id_country`. As a consequence, states of unrelated countries are fetched, and the line `$result[$state['id_country']]['states'][] = $state` silently auto-creates malformed entries containing only a `states` key (no `id_country`, no `name`). When `PS_RESTRICT_DELIVERED_COUNTRIES` is enabled, `CustomerAddressFormatter::getFormat()` iterates this array and emits `Undefined array key "id_country"` / `"name"` warnings (CustomerAddressFormatter.php:100-101), and the FO address form's country dropdown contains broken/extra entries. This PR uses `array_keys($result)` instead, so only states of actually delivered countries are fetched and no phantom entries can be created. Regression introduced in #40044 (shipped since 9.0.2).
resolution.how_to_test: 1. In the BO, go to International > Locations > Countries and enable "Restrict country selections in front office to those covered by active carriers" (`PS_RESTRICT_DELIVERED_COUNTRIES`). 2. Make sure at least one country with a **low ID** and active states (e.g. enable a country whose `id_country` is below the number of delivered countries) is active but **not** covered by any active carrier. 3. In the FO, open the address creation form (My account > Addresses > Create new address). Before the fix: PHP warnings `Undefined array key "id_country"` / `"name"` from `CustomerAddressFormatter.php:100-101` in the logs, and broken/unexpected entries in the country dropdown. After the fix: no warnings, the dropdown lists only carrier-covered countries, and their states load correctly.
resolution.author: paulschwahn

ticket.title: Changing an order's status throws "Duplicate entry '<idp>-<idpa>-0-0' for product_sqlstock" when the order contains a deleted combination (single-shop)
ticket.bug:
On a **single-shop** install (no multistore, no stock sharing, `share_stock = 0`), changing an order's status fails with:

```
[PrestaShopException code 23000] : SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 1062 Duplicate entry '14-183-0-0' for key 'ps_stock_available.product_sqlstock'
```

The error is order-specific: some orders move to the new status fine, others always fail.

**Root cause (investigated):** the failing order contains a **product combination that was later deleted**. `order_detail` still references the old `id_product_attribute` (e.g. `183`), but that combination no longer exists in `product_attribute` / `product_attribute_shop`. When the new status updates stock, `StockManager::getStockAvailableByProduct()` / `StockAvailable::setQuantity()` cannot resolve a shop context for the dead combination and writes a `stock_available` row with `id_shop = 0, id_shop_group = 0`. On a single-shop store this `0-0` row is invalid (it should be `id_shop = 1`). The first qualifying order creates that orphan row; any later order referencing the same deleted combination then collides on the `product_sqlstock` unique key.

Still present (verified in source) in **8.2.6** and **9.1.3**: in `src/Adapter/StockManager::getStockAvailableByProduct()`, when `$id_shop === null` and stock is not shared, `$stockAvailable->id_shop = (int) $id_shop;` evaluates to `0`.
ticket.expected: Changing an order's status should not fail when an order line references a combination that has since been deleted. A `stock_available` row should never be written with `id_shop = 0` on a single-shop install.
ticket.steps:
1. Single-shop install (no multistore).
2. Create a product with a combination (e.g. weight "100 g") → `id_product_attribute = A`.
3. Place an order containing that combination (`order_detail.product_attribute_id = A`).
4. Delete combination `A` from the product (e.g. replace it with another weight).
5. Set that order to a status that updates stock (e.g. "Delivered"). → A `stock_available` row `(product, A, 0, 0)` gets created; this order succeeds.
6. Set another order that also contains combination `A` to that status. → `Duplicate entry '<product>-A-0-0' for key 'product_sqlstock'`.

resolution.title: Fix:  Changing an order's status throws "Duplicate entry '<idp>-<idpa>-0-0' for product_sqlstock" when the order contains a deleted combination (single-shop)
resolution.description: This PR prevents stock movement creation for deleted product combinations by stopping `prepareMovement()` when `productAttributeId > 0` and the related combination no longer exists, using an adapter to avoid direct legacy usage in Core, preventing unintended `stock_available` recreation during order status changes and duplicate key errors.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Single-shop install (no multistore).  Create a product with a combination (e.g. weight "100 g") → id_product_attribute = A.2.   3. Place an order containing that combination (order_detail.product_attribute_id = A).  4. Delete combination A from the product (e.g. replace it with another weight).  5. Set that order to a status that updates stock (e.g. "Delivered"). → The order status is updated successfully and no stock_available row (product, A, 0, 0) is created.  6. Set another order that also contains combination A to that status. → The order status is updated successfully, no duplicate entry error is thrown, and no stock_available row is recreated for the deleted combination.
resolution.author: Codencode

resolution.title: Fix multilang fallback for fields using isRequiredWhenActive and defaultLanguageRequiredWhenActive validators
resolution.description: When a multilang field uses the `isRequiredWhenActive` or `defaultLanguageRequiredWhenActive` validator instead of `required => true`, the fallback mechanism in `ObjectModel::formatFields()` was skipped. This caused non-default languages to be saved as empty strings in the database instead of inheriting the default language value. The CartRule `name` field was changed from `required => true` to `required => false` with `validate => defaultLanguageRequiredWhenActive` in a previous commit (8d3da9f5d6). This broke the fallback, causing blank promo names in FO, exceptions at checkout, and missing order statuses when using a non-default language. The fix extends the fallback condition in `ObjectModel::formatFields()` to also trigger for these two validators, which are semantically equivalent to `required` for the default language value. A Behat regression test is also added to cover this scenario.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Install PrestaShop with two languages (e.g. EN as default + FR). 2. Go to BO > Catalog > Discounts > Add new cart rule. 3. Fill the name **only** in the default language (EN), set a code, enable the rule and add a reduction. 4. Save. 5. Check the `ps_cart_rule_lang` table: the `name` column for FR must contain the EN value, not an empty string. 6. In FO, add a product to cart, switch to FR, apply the promo code → the discount name must appear correctly and checkout must complete without exception. Alternatively, run the Behat test: `./vendor/bin/behat -c tests/Integration/Behaviour/behat.yml -s discount --tags add-cart-level-discount`

ticket.title: Array to string conversion in RenderedHook::outputContent() when legacy modules return hook content
ticket.bug:
A PHP E_WARNING "Array to string conversion" is triggered on every admin page
  that renders a legacy module hook through the Symfony hook dispatcher.

  The warning originates in RenderedHook::outputContent() (line 55) which calls
  implode('', $this->content) expecting string values, but receives arrays.
  This is caused by LegacyHookSubscriber wrapping hook output in a single-element
  array via setContent([content], listener), while HookDispatcher stores the
  result of popContent() — an array — directly into $renderingContent without
  flattening it first.

  In a default PHP setup the warning is silent and "Array" may appear somewhere
  in the rendered HTML (invisible to the user). With any strict error handler
  that converts E_WARNING to exceptions (e.g. a Sentry/monitoring module),
  the admin page crashes entirely.


`E_WARNING: Array to string conversion
  in .../src/Core/Hook/RenderedHook.php on line 55

  #0 [internal]: implode
  #1 .../src/Core/Hook/RenderedHook.php(55): RenderedHook::outputContent
  #2 .../src/PrestaShopBundle/Twig/HookExtension.php(150): HookExtension::renderHook
  #3 .../var/cache/prod/admin/twig/b4/b482833f...php(188): doDisplay
  #4 .../vendor/twig/twig/src/Template.php(402): Twig\Template::yield
  #5 .../vendor/twig/twig/src/Template.php(358): Twig\Template::display
  #6 .../vendor/twig/twig/src/Template.php(373): Twig\Template::render
  #7 .../vendor/symfony/ux-twig-component/src/ComponentRenderer.php(77)
  #8 .../vendor/symfony/ux-twig-component/src/ComponentRenderer.php(56)
  #9 .../vendor/symfony/ux-twig-component/src/Twig/ComponentRuntime.php(51)
  ...
  #N .../src/PrestaShopBundle/Controller/Admin/Improve/ModuleController.php(91)`
ticket.expected:
The hook content returned by legacy modules should render correctly as a
  string in the admin page, with no PHP warning emitted.

  RenderedHook::outputContent() is documented to hold string values
  (['module_name' => 'rendered_content', ...]) and implode() should
  concatenate them without error.

resolution.title: Fix "Array to string conversion" in RenderedHook::outputContent()
resolution.description: A legacy module that returns an **array** instead of a string from a rendering hook causes a PHP `E_WARNING: Array to string conversion` in `RenderedHook::outputContent()`. `Hook::exec(..., $array_return=true)` stores the module output as-is (unlike the non-array path, which discards arrays with a dev notice). After `LegacyHookSubscriber` wraps it once more and the dispatcher's one-level `current()` flatten, a nested array survives down to `implode('', $this->content)`. The warning is silent under PHP's default handler (renders `Array` in the HTML), but crashes the whole admin page under a strict error handler (e.g. a Sentry monitoring module). `outputContent()` now concatenates content recursively, honoring its documented string-output contract regardless of nesting.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Have a legacy module hooked on a back-office rendering hook return an array (instead of a string) from its hook method. 2. With the previous code, loading an admin page (e.g. **Modules > Module Manager**) emits `E_WARNING: Array to string conversion` in `src/Core/Hook/RenderedHook.php` (visible via the PHP error log, or as a hard crash if a strict error handler promotes warnings to exceptions). 3. With this fix, the page renders without any warning and the string parts of the content are concatenated correctly. Automated coverage: `php vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Unit/Core/Hook/RenderedHookTest.php`.
resolution.author: PrestaEdit

resolution.title: Fix states grid not refreshing after toggle when filters are active

ticket.title: Cart rule compatibility search does not filter results for new cart rules
ticket.bug:
In the Back Office, when editing the "Compatible with other cart rules" autocomplete (Catalog → Discounts → new cart rule → Conditions tab → "Compatibility with other cart rules"), typing a term in the search field does not filter the list. All cart rules are returned regardless of what is typed.

This happens whenever the cart rule has no compatibility restriction set yet, i.e.:

when creating a new cart rule (the AJAX call uses id_cart_rule=0), or
when editing an existing cart rule whose cart_rule_restriction = 0.
Root cause is in CartRule::getAssociatedRestrictions() (classes/CartRule.php). When !Validate::isLoadedObject($this) || $this->{$type.'_restriction'} == 0, the method runs an SQL query that never uses the $search_cart_rule_name argument. The LIKE filter on the name only exists in the other branch, reached through getCartRuleCombinations(), which only applies to an already-saved rule with cart_rule_restriction = 1.

Example AJAX request where the search parameter is ignored:

index.php?controller=AdminCartRules&token=...&ajax=1&id_cart_rule=0&action=loadCartRules&limit=40&count=0&type=selected&search=10
ticket.expected: The list is filtered to only the cart rules whose name matches the typed term.
ticket.steps:
1. Go to Catalog → Discounts and create several cart rules with distinct names (e.g. 10% off, -50% summer, Free shipping).
2. Click Add new cart rule and open the Conditions tab.
3. In "Compatibility with other cart rules", type part of a name in the search field (e.g. 10).
4. Observe the suggestions list.

resolution.title: Cart rule compatibility search does not filter results for new cart rule
resolution.description: When editing the "Compatibility with other cart rules" autocomplete (Catalog → Discounts → Cart Rules → tab *Conditions* → "Compatible with other cart rules"), the search field does not filter the list of cart rules. Typing a search term still returns all cart rules instead of those matching the term. This happens whenever the cart rule has no compatibility restriction set yet - i.e. when **creating a new cart rule** (`id_cart_rule=0`) or editing an existing one whose `cart_rule_restriction = 0`.  Root cause: in `CartRule::getAssociatedRestrictions()`, when `!Validate::isLoadedObject($this) \|\| $this->cart_rule_restriction == 0`, the method runs an SQL query that **never applies** the `$search_cart_rule_name` argument. The `LIKE` filter only exists in the other branch, through `getCartRuleCombinations()`, which is reached only for an already-saved rule with `cart_rule_restriction = 1`.  Fix: apply the missing `AND tl.name LIKE "%...%"` filter (escaped via `pSQL()`) in that branch, only for the `cart_rule` type and only when a search term is provided.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Go to **Catalog → Discounts** and create a few cart rules with distinct names (e.g. `10% off`, `-50% summer`, `Free shipping`). 2. Create a **new** cart rule, open the **Conditions** tab, and use the "Compatible with other cart rules" search field. 3. Type part of a name (e.g. `10`). **Before:** the list ignores the term and shows all cart rules. **After:** the list is filtered to cart rules whose name matches the term. 4. Repeat while editing an existing cart rule that has its compatibility restriction disabled - same result.
resolution.author: LaBisquerie

resolution.title: Fix Discount V2 end date validation when period never expires is checked
resolution.description: When creating a discount in Discount V2, if an end date earlier than the start date was entered and then "Period never expires" was checked, the form still raised a validation error on the end date field.    **Root cause (two layers):**   1. **JS**: the `FormFieldToggler` used `ToggleType.visibility` which only hides the field visually (`d-none`) but does not add `disabled` on the inputs — the browser still submits the previous end date value.   2. **PHP**: the `DateRange` constraint in `DiscountPeriodType` is applied unconditionally; there was no `PRE_SUBMIT` listener to clear the end date before Symfony validation when `period_never_expires` is checked.    **Fix:**   - Added a second `FormFieldToggler` with `ToggleType.availability` to disable the end date inputs when "never expires" is checked, preventing submission.   - Added a `PRE_SUBMIT` event listener in `DiscountPeriodType` that sets `valid_date_range.to` to `null` when `period_never_expires` is checked, so the server-side `DateRange` constraint is bypassed even if JS is disabled or bypassed.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Go to BO > Catalog > Discounts > Create a discount   2. Set a name   3. In the Period section, set an end date **earlier** than the start date (e.g. start: tomorrow, end: today)   4. Check **"Period never expires"**   5. Fill in a discount value and save   **Expected:** form saves successfully, no date range error.   **Before fix:** form still showed "The expiration date must be after start date".
resolution.author: mattgoud

ticket.title: Multishop: cache_default_attribute is not reset for all shops when changing a product with combinations to a standard product
ticket.bug:
In a multishop context, when a product has combinations, PrestaShop stores the default combination ID in the `cache_default_attribute` field of the `product_shop` table.

If the product type is later changed from a product with combinations to **Standard product**, the `cache_default_attribute` value is reset to `0` only for the default shop.

Rows related to the other shops keep the previous default combination ID. This leaves inconsistent data in `product_shop` and can trigger a front-office error on the product page.

Error:

```text
Deprecated: round(): Passing null to parameter #1 ($num) of type int|float is deprecated in D:\cms\Prestashop\_Github\PrestaShop-dev-9.1\classes\Tools.php on line 1618
```

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/610d4be6-9225-4ad6-bcde-e6e78bdb3942
ticket.steps:
1. Enable multishop.
2. Create at least two shops.
3. Create a product assigned to both shops.
4. Set the product type to a product with combinations.
5. Create one or more combinations.
6. Set one combination as the default combination.
7. Check the `product_shop` table.
8. Verify that `cache_default_attribute` is populated with the default combination ID for the product shop rows.
9. Edit the product.
10. Change the product type to **Standard product**.
11. Save the product.
12. Check the `product_shop` table again.
13. Notice that `cache_default_attribute` is set to `0` only for the default shop, while the other shop rows still contain the old combination ID.
14. Open the product page in the front office for the affected shop.

resolution.title: Fix: Multishop: cache_default_attribute is not reset for all shops when changing a product with combinations to a standard product
resolution.description: This PR fixes an issue in a multishop context when changing a product with combinations to a standard product. Previously, the product type update was applied only to the product default shop. As a result, some product shop data, such as `cache_default_attribute`, could remain inconsistent for the other shops. The update now uses `ShopConstraint::allShops()` so the product type change is correctly applied to all shops associated with the product.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Enable multishop. 2. Create at least two shops. 3. Create a product assigned to both shops. 4. Set the product as a product with combinations. 5. Create one or more combinations. 6. Set one combination as the default combination. 7. Change the product type to **Standard product**. 8. Save the product. 9. Check the `product_shop` table for the product. 10. Confirm that `cache_default_attribute` is set to `0` for all shops. 11. Open the product page in the front office for each shop. 12. Confirm that the product page is displayed correctly and no deprecated warning is triggered.
resolution.author: Codencode

resolution.title: Fix: [Multishop] Error when updating "Schema of URLs" for a single shop
resolution.description: In multishop context, the URL schema form contains additional fields prefixed with `multistore_`. These fields are boolean values used to determine whether a specific field is being overridden for the current shop. ticket.title: Invalid product URLs trigger Fatal in ProductController::assignPriceAndTax (PHP 8 / PS 9)
ticket.bug:
`ProductController::initContent()` unconditionally calls `assignPriceAndTax()` without checking whether `$this->product` is a loaded object. When the product cannot be loaded (deleted, inactive, invalid id in the URL), `init()` already
 handled the case by setting the 404 template and returning , but `Controller::run()` keeps going and calls `initContent()` anyway, leading to a Fatal error.

**Call chain:**
```
Controller::run() [classes/controller/Controller.php:308]
  → ProductController::initContent() [controllers/front/ProductController.php:306]
    → ProductController::assignPriceAndTax() [line 529]
       → crash on line 536 (getTaxesRate on null) OR line 539 (getPriceStatic with null id)
```

**Two observable crash points:**

- `ProductController.php:536` , `$this->product->getTaxesRate(...)` → Fatal `Call to a member function getTaxesRate() on null` when `$this->product === null` (URL has `id_product=0` or missing id).
- `ProductController.php:539` , `Product::getPriceStatic($this->product->id, ...)` → `PrestaShopException('Product ID is invalid.')` when `$this->product` is a non-loaded Product object (`new Product(XXXXX)` where the id doesn't exist
returns an object with `id = null`).

**Why `init()` doesn't prevent it:** `init()` correctly detects the invalid product (line 133) and calls `setTemplate('errors/404'); return;`, but the `return` only exits `init()`, not `run()`. `Controller::run()` proceeds to call
`initContent()` regardless.

**Why this is a PHP 8 regression:** PS 1.7 / PS 8 `ProductController` had the same logical flaw, but PHP 7 tolerated `null->method()` with a silent warning. PHP 8 turns it into a `TypeError`.

**Real-world impact:** on any production store with indexed URLs, search engine crawlers (Google, Bing, Facebook) continuously hit URLs of deleted/renamed products. On our store (540k orders, 50k+ products, multilingual) this produces
~40 `*ERROR* Product ID is invalid` entries per hour in `var/logs/<YYYYMMDD>_exception.log`, plus occasional 500s in Apache error log. Zero functional impact (caught exceptions are silenced upstream for most code paths), but the log
noise drowns out legitimate errors.
ticket.expected: A request to a non-existent or deleted product URL should return HTTP 404 rendered via the `errors/404` template that `init()` already selected, with no Fatal error, no PrestaShopException, and no entry in `exception.log`.
ticket.steps:
1. On any PS 9 install, hit a URL of a non-existent or deleted product, e.g.:
   ```
   https://<shop>/<lang>/999999-nonexistent.html
   https://<shop>/<lang>/<id_of_deleted_product>-<old-slug>.html
   ```
2. Browser receives `HTTP 500`.
3. Check `var/logs/<YYYYMMDD>_exception.log` and `/var/log/apache2/error.log`:
   - `PHP Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to a member function getTaxesRate() on null in controllers/front/ProductController.php:536`
   - And/or `*ERROR* Product ID is invalid. at line 3363 in file classes/Product.php`
4. Stack trace consistently terminates at `ProductController::assignPriceAndTax()` → `initContent()` → `Controller::run()`.

resolution.title: Guard product page when product is null
resolution.description: This PR adds a null guard around product-dependent logic in `ProductController` to avoid errors when the product is not available or not properly initialized. It ensures methods like `initContent()` and breadcrumb generation do not try to access product data when `$this->product` is `null`, making the product page flow more robust in invalid or edge-case contexts.

ticket.title: CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder() always returns 1 instead of the true total
ticket.bug:
`CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` always returns `1` as the country count, regardless of how many countries exist in the database.

The root cause is that `->groupBy('c.id_country')` is placed in the shared `getQueryBuilder()` method (`src/Core/Grid/Query/CountryQueryBuilder.php`, line 106), which is called by **both** `getSearchQueryBuilder()` and `getCountQueryBuilder()`. The count query therefore inherits `GROUP BY`, becoming:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)
FROM ps_country c
INNER JOIN ps_country_lang cl ON cl.id_country = c.id_country AND cl.id_lang = 1
INNER JOIN ps_zone z ON z.id_zone = c.id_zone
INNER JOIN ps_country_shop cs ON c.id_country = cs.id_country AND cs.id_shop IN (1)
GROUP BY c.id_country;
```

This returns one row per country, each with value `1`. `DoctrineGridDataFactory::fetchOne()` picks the first row → the total is always `1`.
ticket.expected: `getCountQueryBuilder()` should return a single row with the true total number of countries (e.g. `241`), so that any consumer of `DoctrineGridDataFactory` with the country grid receives the correct `totalItems`.
ticket.steps:
1. Install PrestaShop with the default country dataset.
2. Run the following SQL against your database (replace `id_lang` and `id_shop` with your actual values):

```sql
-- Find your values:
SELECT id_lang FROM ps_lang WHERE active = 1 LIMIT 1;
SELECT id_shop FROM ps_shop WHERE active = 1 LIMIT 1;

-- Buggy count query (as generated by getCountQueryBuilder):
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)
FROM ps_country c
INNER JOIN ps_country_lang cl ON cl.id_country = c.id_country AND cl.id_lang = 1
INNER JOIN ps_zone z ON z.id_zone = c.id_zone
INNER JOIN ps_country_shop cs ON c.id_country = cs.id_country AND cs.id_shop IN (1)
GROUP BY c.id_country;
```

3. Observe that the query returns **241 rows, each containing `1`**, instead of a single row with `241`.
4. Confirm by inspecting `CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` in `src/Core/Grid/Query/CountryQueryBuilder.php` — `groupBy('c.id_country')` is inherited from `getQueryBuilder()`.

resolution.title: Fix: CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder() always returns 1 instead of the true total
resolution.description: This PR fixes the country grid total count calculation. `CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` was reusing a base query that already contained `GROUP BY c.id_country`, causing the count query to return multiple rows with value `1` instead of a single row with the real total. The `GROUP BY` is now applied only to the search query, while the count query keeps using `COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)` without grouping.  This keeps the country list deduplicated in multistore contexts and restores the correct `totalItems` value for the grid.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Enable the experimental **"Countries"** feature in **Advanced Parameters > New & Experimental Features**. 2. Go to **International > Locations > Countries**. 3. Check that the total displayed in the table header matches the actual number of countries and is **not `1`**.
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Uploading logo in Design -> Theme & Logo in multistore with a single shop selected causes TypeError with PHP 8.3
ticket.bug:
Updating a logo, mail logo or invoice in multistore with single shop selected causes TypeError with PHP 8.3 and crashes. 

**TypeError**
_ShopCore::getGroupIdFromShopId(): Argument #1 ($shopId) must be of type int, null given, called in ../prestashop/classes/shop/Shop.php on line 1015_

This issue also causes **ShopException** _Shop group id 0 is invalid. Shop group id must be a number that is greater than zero._



Culprit is `\PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Shop\LogoUploader::updateInMultiShopContext`  that calls `Shop::setContext(Shop::CONTEXT_SHOP);` without `$idShop` as second argument even though it is readily available. Without `$idShop` `\ShopCore::setContext` tries to call `Shop::getGroupIdFromShopId($id)` with $id value of null and getGroupIdFromShopId is defined with typehint int.
I searched the project and luckily didn't find any other invalid calls to `Shop::setContext(Shop::CONTEXT_SHOP);` without Shop ID so just adding idShop as argument should be enough.

`\PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Shop\LogoUploader::updateInMultiShopContext` also makes couple of calls `Shop::setContext(Shop::CONTEXT_GROUP);` without second `$id` argument that is also available in the same function. Therefore that is probably not working as intended and might cause some issues, but I didn't get in that deep.

ticket.title: Bug: reserved_quantity not updated when "Share available quantities for sale" is enabled (Multishop)
ticket.bug:
In a multishop environment with 2 shops in the same shop group, when the option:

**Shop Group → Share available quantities for sale**

is enabled (`true`),

product quantities are shared between shops.

However, when placing an order, the system does not correctly update the `reserved_quantity` field in the `stock_available` table.

This happens because in this situation, the `stock_available` records have `id_shop = 0`, but the `PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Adapter::updateReservedProductQuantity()` method performs the update by passing `id_shop = ID_SHOP` (e.g., `id_shop = 1`). Therefore, the query does not match any row in stock_available.

As a result, `reserved_quantity` is never updated.

When the order status changes to **Shipped**: `physical_quantity` is never recalculated correctly.
ticket.steps:
- Enable multishop.
- Create a shop group with:
  - 2 shops
  - "Share available quantities for sale" = true
-  Create a product with stock.
- Place an order in one shop.
-  Check the `stock_available` table and verify that the `reserved_quantity` field has not changed (it remains 0), while it should be updated with the purchased quantity.

resolution.title: Fix: Bug: reserved_quantity not updated when "Share available quantities for sale" is enabled (Multishop)
resolution.description: When multishop is enabled and "Share available quantities for sale" is set to true, the stock_available row is stored with id_shop = 0.  However, `updateReservedProductQuantity()` was using the current shop ID, causing the UPDATE query to not match any row. This resulted in reserved_quantity not being updated and `physical_quantity` never being recalculated properly. This fix resolves the correct stock shop ID (0 when `share_stock `is enabled) before executing the update query.
resolution.how_to_test: TEST 1 - Enable multishop. - Create a shop group with: 2 shops and shop group with field **Share available quantities for sale** = true - Create a product with stock. - Place an order in one shop. - Check the `stock_available` table and verify that the `reserved_quantity` field has been updated with the purchased quantity. - Change the order status to "Shipped" and verify that the `physical_quantity` field has been updated accordingly. TEST 2 - Create 2 shop groups, each with 2 shops and with field **Share available quantities for sale** = true. - Create a product with stock assigned to both shop groups. - Place an order in one shop of the first group and verify that `reserved_quantity` is updated only for that shop group (id_shop = 0 within the group scope). - Ensure that stock values of the second shop group remain unchanged.
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Category::searchByPath loses parent context after creating missing segment
ticket.bug:
When Category::searchByPath() creates a missing category segment via the $objectToCreate callback, the subsequent recursive call loses parent context. This can cause the next lookup to resolve the wrong category when identical names exist under different parents, or prevent correct path traversal.

The method is designed to recurse, but it currently recurses using only the segment name instead of the accumulated path.

Actual behavior
The method recurses using only the current segment name:
Category::searchByPath($idLang, $categoryName);
This drops the accumulated path and parent context.

Root cause
The recursive call uses the segment name instead of the accumulated path (path-so-far), causing loss of $idParentCategory context.
ticket.expected: After creating a missing path segment, searchByPath() should continue recursion using the full path up to the created segment, preserving parent context for subsequent lookups.
ticket.steps:
Create the following categories:

A (under root)

Other/A (same name under a different parent)

Call: Category::searchByPath($idLang, 'Other/A/NewChild', $creatorObject, $creatorMethod);
where NewChild does not exist and is created by the callback.

Observe that after creating NewChild, the recursion can resolve the wrong parent or fail to continue traversal correctly.

resolution.title: Fix Category::searchByPath losing context during recursion
resolution.description: Fixes loss of parent context in `Category::searchByPath()` when creating missing path segments. The method recurses using only the segment name, which discards the accumulated path and can resolve incorrect parents when category names are duplicated. This change preserves recursion semantics by recursing with the accumulated path. |
resolution.how_to_test: 1) Create categories: `A` (root) and `Other/A`. 2) Call `Category::searchByPath($idLang, 'Other/A/NewChild', $creator, $method)` where `NewChild` does not exist. 3) Verify `NewChild` is created under `Other/A` and returned correctly. |

ticket.title: CsvFileReader service fails with "You have requested a non-existent service 'session'"
ticket.bug: When trying to use the service `prestashop.core.import.csv_file_reader`, which points to the class `PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Import\File\CsvFileReader`, the following error occurs: `You have requested a non-existent service "session"` A screenshot of the error is attached.
ticket.steps:
1. Install the module [issue_csvfilereader.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24719955/issue_csvfilereader.zip)
2. Go to the module configuration page
3. The error is displayed immediately

resolution.title: Fix: CsvFileReader service fails with "You have requested a non-existent service 'session'"
resolution.description: This PR fixes an issue in the `prestashop.core.import.csv_file_reader` service definition where the `session` service was accessed directly, causing a `"You have requested a non-existent service 'session'"` error in certain contexts.  The service definition has been updated to retrieve the session via `RequestStack`. This issue did not occur in PrestaShop 8 because the `session` service was still available.   Starting from **Symfony 5.3**, the direct `session` service has been deprecated and later removed in favor of accessing the session through `RequestStack`.  See: https://symfony.com/blog/new-in-symfony-5-3-session-service-deprecation
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Install the module [issue_csvfilereader.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24719955/issue_csvfilereader.zip)  2. Go to the module configuration page 3. You should no longer see the error.

ticket.title: Module update problem
ticket.bug: If you create an update for a module and in the update there is a need to hook/unhook the module from a hook, it doesn't work because the instance of the object (module) passed to the update function does not have the "id" attribute set.
ticket.steps:
1. Install the [issue40429.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24384071/issue40429.zip) module, which will be attached to the hookDisplayBackOfficeTop hook.
2. Go to the configuration and you will see: `This module is registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop`.
3. Open the issue40429.php file and change
`$this->version = '1.0.0'` to `$this->version = '1.0.1'`.
4. Now go to _Module > Module Manager > Updates_.
5. Update the module. During the update, the system will "attempt" to detach the module from the `hookDisplayBackOfficeTop `hook.
6. Now go back to the module configuration, and you will still see: `This module is registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop` — instead, you should see: `This module is NOT registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop`.

resolution.title: Fix: Module update problem
resolution.description: Since PrestaShop 9.0.2, the Modules page has been migrated to Symfony (see https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/36845), so module updates are now executed under a Symfony controller.  As the controller is no longer a legacy Controller, the Module constructor always resets the modules cache via `static::$modules_cache = null;`, because the following condition is always satisfied:  ```php if (!$this->context->controller instanceof Controller) {```  This PR prevents the modules cache from being reset in this context, ensuring module updates work correctly.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Install the [issue40429.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24384071/issue40429.zip) module, which will be attached to the hookDisplayBackOfficeTop hook. 2. Go to the configuration and you will see: `This module is registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop`. 3. Open the issue40429.php file and change `$this->version = '1.0.0'` to `$this->version = '1.0.1'`. 4. Now go to _Module > Module Manager > Updates_. 5. Update the module. During the update, the system will "attempt" to detach the module from the `hookDisplayBackOfficeTop `hook. 6. Now go back to the module configuration, you should see: `This module is NOT registered on hookDisplayBackOfficeTop`.
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Issue retrieving product price when adding the first specific_price
ticket.bug:
When a new **specific_price** is added and no other specific prices exist in the catalog, the product price retrieved inside the `hookActionObjectSpecificPriceAddAfter` hook does not take the newly added discount into account.

This happens because the configuration `PS_SPECIFIC_PRICE_FEATURE_ACTIVE` is set to 1 only after the specific_price is created. However, the `hookActionObjectSpecificPriceAddAfterhook` is executed before this configuration is updated.
As a result, when the hook attempts to retrieve the product price, the feature is still disabled (`NULL`) and the discount is not applied.
ticket.expected: The price retrieved inside the hook should correctly reflect the newly added specific_price, even when it is the first specific_price in the catalog.
ticket.steps:
1. Install the module [issue40255.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23959265/issue40255.zip).
2. Ensure that no specific prices exist in the catalog.
3. Open a product in edit mode.
4. In the Pricing section, add a new specific price.
5. When the popup reloads, you will see the message (added by the module): `Product price: FULL_PRICE Reduction: 0`
Instead, the price should reflect the applied discount, and **Reduction** should be different from 0.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/729963bf-689f-4cd9-86ae-633bb3549355

resolution.title: Fix: Issue retrieving product price when adding the first specific_price
resolution.description: This PR ensures that `PS_SPECIFIC_PRICE_FEATURE_ACTIVE` is enabled before inserting the first specific price, allowing hooks to correctly retrieve discounted prices. If the insertion fails, the previous configuration value is restored to avoid leaving the system in an inconsistent state.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Install the module [issue40255.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23959265/issue40255.zip).  2. Ensure that no specific prices exist in the catalog.  3. Open a product in edit mode.  4. In the Pricing section, add a new specific price.  5. When the popup reloads, you will see the message (added by the module): `Product price: DISCOUNTED_PRICE Reduction: REDUCTION`   You need to display the discounted price and the discount amount
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Cart rule combinations lost when saving if lazy-loaded list (jscroll) is not fully loaded
ticket.bug:
When editing a cart rule with a large number of “compatible cart rules”, the Back Office loads the list using *infinite scroll* (`jscroll`), but **only the currently loaded items are included in the `<select name="cart_rule_select[]>` POST payload**.

Because of this, when saving a cart rule **without scrolling the list to the end**, PrestaShop deletes *all* existing combinations for that rule (as part of the normal `afterUpdate` process), then recreates them only from the partial list sent in the form.

This leads to **data loss**: most combinations disappear permanently after the user saves the rule.

This affects both:

- existing combinations loaded from DB,
- new combinations added via AJAX,
- any combinations not currently loaded in the DOM at save time.

This is a **core data integrity bug** caused by BO lazy-loading in file [conditions.tpl](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/65e40453e0478cf5472093b69ae567d0d2b5d6b4/admin-dev/themes/default/template/controllers/cart_rules/conditions.tpl#L271) + how PrestaShop reconstructs cart rule combinations after update.
ticket.expected:
Saving a cart rule **should not delete combinations that were not visible in the DOM** due to lazy-loading.

Either:

- the UI should send **all existing combination IDs**, not only loaded items,  
**or**
- the backend should preserve existing combinations instead of deleting them blindly.
ticket.steps:
1. Create a large number of cart rules (e.g. 1000+).
2. Edit any cart rule that has many combinable rules.
3. In the “Conditions” tab, the list of combinable rules is rendered using `jscroll` and loads items in batches via AJAX infinite scroll.
4. Do **not** scroll to the bottom — leave most combinations not loaded.
5. Click **Save**.
6. PrestaShop removes all combinations:
   ```sql
   DELETE FROM cart_rule_combination 
   WHERE id_cart_rule_1 = X OR id_cart_rule_2 = X
   ```
7. PrestaShop recreates combinations only from:
   ```
   POST['cart_rule_select[]']
   ```
   — which contains **only the few rules loaded at the top**.
8. The majority of combinations are lost.

resolution.title: Fix: Cart rule combinations lost when saving if lazy-loaded list (jscroll) is not fully loaded
resolution.description: This PR fixes how cart rule combinations are saved when using an AJAX-loaded select. Previously only the options loaded in the dropdown were considered, so combinations could be incomplete if the user didn’t scroll the list. The form now submits the list of unselected cart rules, and the backend derives the selected ones from the full set, ensuring all intended combinations are stored correctly.

ticket.title: Order::getIdByCartId in OrderConfirmationControllerCore fails to query order_id when cached
ticket.bug:
When a payment module redirects to order-confirmation, the `OrderId` is fetched using:
`$this->id_order = Order::getIdByCartId((int) $this->id_cart);` https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/1d97fcde1bf31d522cfbcfde904316da1d9088d6/controllers/front/OrderConfirmationController.php#L83

`Order::getIdByCartId` uses `$result = Db::getInstance()->getValue($sql);`, with the default of getValue being to use cache.
Now, in some clustered environments it's possible that the order is created by one node and the confirmation page is server by another; this seems to cause the `Order::getIdByCartId` to return a cached `false`, causing the confirmation page to do an early redirect, exiting early. https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/1d97fcde1bf31d522cfbcfde904316da1d9088d6/controllers/front/OrderConfirmationController.php#L95

In my experiments, forcing `Order::getIdByCartId` to query a non cached result solves the issue.
ticket.steps:
1. Pay an order with a PSP that confirms the payment via S2S callbacks.
2. If the conditions align you will sometimes get redirected away from the confirmation page

resolution.title: Always request a non cached result in Order::getIdByCartId
resolution.description: This resolves an issue with the order-confirmation controller evident in clustered environments using cache. (see #40007)
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Deploy in a clustered environment with APCu cache enabled. 2. Enable a payment module which receives the payment validation via server-to-server communication from the PSP 3. Place an order, pay and get redirected to confirmation page (before the fix you sometimes will get redirected away from the order confirmation page |
resolution.author: ilsalvopss

ticket.title: Category link cache doesn't take shopId as a parameter
ticket.bug:
While working on a `hreflang` generation module, when generating alternate URL's for products, I noticed that product URL with the default category inside was wrong. While the actual `link_rewrite` of the product with shopId and langId is valid, the category `link_rewrite` was only taking langId into account, as a result, if a category present in multiple shops has a different `link_rewrite` for a same given language, it will never be reflected in the URL.

Example :
2 shops (1 and 2) with only one language being English (1)
A category shared in both shops
`link_rewrite` for shop 1 language 1 - "my-nice-category"
`link_rewrite` for shop 2 language 1 - "my-very-nice-category"

A product shared in both shops
`link_rewrite` for shop 1 language 1 - "my-nice-product"
`link_rewrite` for shop 1 language 1 - "my-very-nice-product"

If we generate the product URL using the `Link` object, in the same HTTP request will give:
Shop 1 language 1 - `https://example.shop/my-nice-category/1-my-nice-product`
Shop 2 language 1 - `https://example.shop/my-nice-category/1-my-very-nice-product`

Cause of this behavior:
```php
    public static function getLinkRewrite($idCategory, $idLang)
    {
        if (!Validate::isUnsignedId($idCategory) || !Validate::isUnsignedId($idLang)) {
            return false;
        }

        if (!isset(self::$_links[$idCategory . '-' . $idLang])) { // < Here, this static cache, ignoring shopId
            self::$_links[$idCategory . '-' . $idLang] = Db::getInstance()->getValue('
			SELECT cl.`link_rewrite`
			FROM `' . _DB_PREFIX_ . 'category_lang` cl
			WHERE `id_lang` = ' . (int) $idLang . '
			' . Shop::addSqlRestrictionOnLang('cl') . '
			AND cl.`id_category` = ' . (int) $idCategory);
        }

        return self::$_links[$idCategory . '-' . $idLang];
    }
```

Note: PR pending
ticket.expected:
Shop 1 language 1 - `https://example.shop/my-nice-category/1-my-nice-product`
Shop 2 language 1 - `https://example.shop/my-very-nice-category/1-my-very-nice-product`
ticket.steps:
Any version of Prestashop (Oldest one checked is 1.7)

- Enable multistore
- Create a second store
- Create a category in `All` context, then edit the `URL` to a different one in the context of the second shop
- Create a product in `All` context
- Test the URL generation

resolution.title: Add idShop cache value for getLinkRewrite Category and Category CMS
resolution.description: Category link cache doesn't take shopId as a parameter
resolution.author: Touxten

ticket.title: Missing Content-Type header in stock quantity update request
ticket.bug: When updating product quantities from the admin panel, the outgoing POST request does not include the Content-Type: application/json header, even though the request body is JSON. On servers with ModSecurity enabled, such requests are blocked with a 403 Forbidden error because they appear to contain JSON but lack the appropriate content type header.
ticket.steps:
1. Enable ModSecurity on your server
2. Go to Catalog -> Stock in the back office
3. Try to update the product quantity by using single or bulk action
4. HTTP 403 error occurs when making a POST request to /index.php/api/stocks/products

resolution.title: Add missing Content-Type header in stock quantity update request
resolution.description: When updating product quantities from the admin panel, the outgoing POST request does not include the Content-Type: application/json header, even though the request body is JSON. On servers with ModSecurity enabled, such requests are blocked with a 403 Forbidden error because they appear to contain JSON but lack the appropriate content type header. This PR adds Content-Type headers for stock management update requests.
resolution.how_to_test: Enable ModSecurity on your server. Go to Catalog -> Stock and update product quantity (both by using single item and bulk action)
resolution.author: nborkowska

ticket.title: Calling delete() method on an empty instance of Customer object leads to the deletion of all non-customer-restricted specific prices
ticket.bug:
Calling the delete() method on an empty instance of Customer ObjectModel leads to the deletion **of all** the shop's specific prices that are not restricted to any customer (id_customer = 0).
This corresponds to the majority of specific prices in most cases, so this issue is quite annoying and can have dramatic consequences for the shop sales and marketing campaigns if it happens and is not addressed quickly by restoring a backup.

**This issue is present in all versions of PrestaShop.**
ticket.expected: When calling the delete() method on an instance of Customer object, we should first validate that the passed Customer ID is not empty before processing the deletion of the customer's specific prices.

resolution.title: Ensure specific prices are deleted safely on customer deletion by validating passed ID
resolution.description: Read below
resolution.how_to_test: 1. In the back office, add one or more specific prices (to any product) without specifying a customer restriction (applicable to all customer) 2. Anywhere in the code (e.g., in the initContent of IndexController or in the displayHeader hook of a module), add following code : `(new Customer())->delete();` 3. Reload the page corresponding to where you put previous code (e.g., the home page in FO) 4. Go back in BO to the product on which you created the specific prices => they should still exist (before fix, they would have been deleted)
resolution.author: gilles-knani

resolution.title: Fix query builder to find translations by key in Backoffice during the translations saving process
resolution.description: This PR fixes some rare cases where the saving of some translations are impossible using the Backoffice interface. Specifically, whenever you had two or more similar (starting with the same text) translation keys within the same domain, where each one is using a % character (eg. '%s') in their key, this will create an unwanted behaviour where you will be able to traslate just one key, because the query will pull a result everytime since it's using LIKE with the special %s character. I'm proposing to change the LIKE operator to an equal sign, since we must find the exact match by translation key.
resolution.how_to_test: Create two similar translations keys within the same domain, either in a .tpl file or in a module (doesn't matter). Eg: "Hello %s, welcome back" and "Hello %s". Try to translate them.
resolution.author: mcaldex

ticket.title: Issue with JS and CSS cache clearing in multishop context
ticket.bug:
In a multishop environment with at least two stores, when enabling JavaScript or CSS caching (_Advanced Parameters > Performance > CCC (Combine, Compress, and Cache) > Smart cache for JavaScript / Smart cache for CSS_), an issue occurs when clearing the cache.

When the cache is cleared, the system increments the `PS_CCCCSS_VERSION` and `PS_CCCJS_VERSION` configurations based on the selected shop context. However:

- If the operation is performed while selecting a **single shop**, the configurations are correctly updated only for that specific shop.
- If the cache is cleared while selecting "**All stores**", the system updates only the global configurations and not those of individual shops.

As a result, if the cache was previously cleared for a single shop and then cleared again globally, the individual shop’s configurations are not updated. This causes the front-office to use outdated assets, leading to display and loading issues.
ticket.steps:
1. Enable Multishop:
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Multistore and enable the multishop feature.
    - Create at least two shops.

2. Enable JS and CSS Caching:
    - Navigate to Advanced Parameters > Performance.
    - Under the CCC (Combine, Compress, and Cache) section, enable:
        -  Smart cache for JavaScript
        -  Smart cache for CSS
    - Save the settings.
3. Clear Cache for a Single Shop:
    -  In the multishop selector (top-left of the back office), select a single shop.
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Performance and click Clear cache.
    - This will update the "PS_CCCJS_VERSION" and "PS_CCCJS_VERSION" values for the selected shop.
4. Clear Cache for All Shops:
    - In the multishop selector, choose "All stores".
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Performance and click Clear cache again.
    - This updates only the global configurations but does not affect individual shop configurations.
5. Check the Issue in the Front-Office:
    - Visit the front-office of the previously selected single shop.
    - The shop continues to load outdated JavaScript and CSS assets instead of the refreshed ones.

resolution.title: Fix: Issue with JS and CSS cache clearing in multishop context
resolution.description: see https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/38135
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: [Bug] Missing attributes autoplay, loop, muted, and playsinline in the video tag within Tools::purifyHTML()
ticket.bug:
Currently, the `Tools::purifyHTML()` function defines the <video> element with the following allowed attributes:
- src
- type
- width
- height
- poster
- preload
- controls

However, the following attributes are missing:
- autoplay
- loop
- muted
- playsinline

These attributes are essential for the proper functioning of HTML5 videos, especially for:
- Allowing autoplay (necessary for, for example, background videos);
- Enabling loop;
- Ensuring silent autoplay (as required by browsers);
- Enabling inline playback on mobile devices (avoiding the transition to fullscreen).
ticket.steps:
1. Enable the "Use HTMLPurifier Library" option in the PrestaShop back office.
2. In  cms page insert anHTML block containing the following code:
 ```html
<video autoplay="autoplay" loop="loop" muted="muted" playsinline="playsinline">
    <source src="VIDEO_URL" type="video/mp4">
</video>
```
3. Save the content.
4. Observe that the resulting code is "cleaned", with the desired attributes removed:
 ```html
<video>
    <source src="VIDEO_URL" type="video/mp4">
</video>
```

Do you think it would make sense to enable these attributes? I could create a PR regarding this.

Thank you.

resolution.title: Fix: [Bug] Missing attributes autoplay, loop, muted, and playsinline in the video tag within Tools::purifyHTML()
resolution.description: see: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/37967

ticket.title: Multishop: Deleting and recreating a combination removes the shared reference (new Product Page V2)
ticket.bug:
In a multishop setup with two shops (e.g., **B2C** and **B2B**), using the new product page (Product Page v2), if a product has an active combination for both shops, the following behavior occurs:

The product has an active combination with:
**Size**: S
**Reference**: REFERENCE

If I delete this combination from the **B2B** shop and then recreate it, the system reassigns the same combination (keeping the same ID). This behavior is correct and useful.

Issue: During this process, the system removes the value of the **Reference** (reference) field of the combination. Since the **Reference** field is unique across all shops, it should remain unchanged even after deleting and recreating the combination.

In my opinion, the system should preserve the reference value to avoid data loss and ensure proper management of combinations in a multishop context.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa953118-81a5-4c49-b6b3-38bbe4b77241
ticket.expected: The system should retain the value of the **Reference** (REFERENCE) field.
ticket.steps:
1. Set up a multishop configuration with at least two shops (e.g., B2C and B2B).
2. Create a product with an active combination shared across both shops:
**Size**: S
**Reference**: REFERENCE
3. Delete the combination from the B2B shop.
4. Recreate the same combination in the B2B shop.

resolution.title: Fix: Multishop: Deleting and recreating a combination removes the shared reference (new Product Page V2)
resolution.description: see: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/37840 - Note: The issue also occurs on the 9.0.x branch, so I performed the rebase by moving the PR to 9.0.x because PRs are no longer being merged on version 8.2.x.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Set up a multishop configuration with at least two shops (e.g., B2C and B2B). 2. Create a product with an active combination shared across both shops: Size: S Reference: REFERENCE 3. Delete the combination from the B2B shop. 4. Recreate the same combination in the B2B shop. 5. Check that the combination has **REFERENCE** as its reference.  For more info see: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/37840
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Currency conversion is run even if there is set a specific price for a currency
ticket.bug:
When a merchant has 2 or more currencies, one can set a currency conversion. Lets say NOK and EUR. 
NOK is default price and EUR is set to conversion 0,1, meaning a product priced to 100 NOK, should be converted to 10 EUR. This works fine. 

But when a merchant wants to set the price for EUR specifically, lets say he/she sets it to 8 EUR with a specific price, the automatic currency conversion **should not apply**, however it does. 

In this case the price 8 EUR would be converted to 0,8 EUR.
ticket.expected: When specific price is set for a currency, automatic currency conversion should not apply.
ticket.steps:
1. Create a product.
2. Activate two or more currencies, set up  currency conversion numbers.
3. Observe in front office that the price change as expected with automatic currency conversion.
4. Now go to the product and set a specific price for a currency.
5. Observe in front office that BOTH your "manual" specific price currency conversion AND the automatic currency conversion is applied.


Now, here is the sollution:
```
classes/Product.php:3896
$id_currency == $specific_price['id_currency'] // instead of strict check $id_currency === $specific_price['id_currency']
```

6. Now observe it works as it should.

The reason is that `$id_currency` is a string and `$specific_price['id_currency']`  is an int (or the other way, I cant remember), so the typesafe condition fails.

The bug should possibly be solved by making sure both those variables are int`s, but a quick fix is to disable the typecheck.

resolution.title: Fix Incorrect SpecificPrice Currency Conversion (Issue 36844)
resolution.description: Specific Prices have a currency conversion applied to them even if the currency has been set and no conversion is necessary. See issue for full details.
resolution.how_to_test: For a product set a "Specific Price" that does not use the default shop currency and view the item in the store in the same currency. If an exchange rate is set then the price should still match the one set in the back office and the exchange rate will not be applied.
resolution.author: mrkalchemy

ticket.title: Incompatibility Issue with PDO Returning Integer Values with PHP 8.1
ticket.bug:
When using PHP 8.1 with PrestaShop 8.0 (minimal version that support PHP 8.1), the function executeS() from the Db class returns integers for columns that are defined as tinyInt or unsignedInt in the database. In previous PHP versions (before 8.1), the values returned were always strings, regardless of the column type.

This change in behavior is due to PHP 8.1 no longer automatically casting values to strings. Unfortunately, many modules have historically relied on these values being returned as strings, which causes issues when comparing values like '1' === 1.

As a result, module integrations expecting stringified values are disrupted, leading to compatibility issues across PrestaShop versions that support PHP 8.1.

This breaking change is documented here : https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration81.incompatible.php#migration81.incompatible.pdo.sqlite

Exemple with Db->executeS() on ps_product table. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a232848-bedd-488d-a0a7-f4268b9e220d)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c97d0c1f-286f-40a4-bd96-6d68057fb8b1)
ticket.expected:
The "PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES" parameter should be set to true on the PDO instance to maintain the historical behavior and avoid breaking changes.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab8f0b3b-04a1-4532-b58c-efcf70b33296)

resolution.title: Add attr_stringify_fetches to PDO init config to avoid BC Break
resolution.description: Fix Incompatibility Issue with PDO Returning Integer Values with PHP 8.1
resolution.how_to_test: dump a response from database returned by PDO, and check type of values.
resolution.author: fox-john

ticket.title: Problems OrderProductForViewing "must be of type string (or int), null given" and Memcached
ticket.bug:
I had a problem with retrieving the stock location for products that are no longer available when viewing an old order. Normally, this should return false when the stock location is not found. But when the Memcached cache is active, the null value is returned, causing a fatal error. This must be linked to the fact that Memcached doesn't distinguish between null and false. 

To correct my specific problem, I added the following processing at the end of the setProductCurrentStock() method in /classes/order/Order.php:
```
if ($product['location'] === null) {
    $product['location'] = false;
}
```

This ensures that false is returned and not null. 

The following issues seem to be affected by a similar bug: 
[#22215](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/22215)
[#35753](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/35753)
[#35979](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/35979)
ticket.steps:
1. Enable Memcached cache
2. Create an order
3. Delete an ordered product from the catalog
4. View order

resolution.title: Cast OrderProductForViewing - location to string for Memcached
